intent.raw_query: Portugal Algarve, $2200, beach holiday with wine tasting, September 2026 from London

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail from Benagil and descend to the secluded cove for swimming and snorkeling among rock arches.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour
experiences.description: Visit local wineries in the Lagoa DOC wine region, the heart of Algarve winemaking. Tour the vineyards, learn about indigenous grape varieties like Negra Mole and Crato Branco, and enjoy guided tastings of regional whites, reds, and the famous Algarve medronho brandy paired with local cheeses.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle by kayak through the iconic Benagil Cave, one of the most photographed sea caves in the world. A guided tour takes you through hidden grottos, natural arches, and secluded beaches only accessible by water, offering a unique perspective of the Algarve's dramatic coastline.

experiences.name: Sagres Sunset & Cape St. Vincent Visit
experiences.description: Travel to the southwestern tip of Europe at Cape St. Vincent, a windswept promontory with a historic lighthouse and breathtaking Atlantic views. Explore the nearby Sagres Fortress, steeped in Age of Discovery history, and stay for one of the most spectacular sunsets on the continent.

experiences.name: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat & Seafood Experience
experiences.description: Take a guided boat tour through the Ria Formosa lagoon system, a protected natural park teeming with wildlife and barrier islands. Stop at a traditional oyster and clam farm for a tasting straight from the water, then visit the pristine Ilha Deserta beach, accessible only by boat.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Portugal Algarve
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Take the affordable Aerobus or local bus to your accommodation at Aegean Bliss Resort in the Algarve beachfront area. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented with your surroundings.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack at a nearby convenience store or a local 24-hour cafe near the resort - try a Bifana (pork sandwich) or Pastel de Nata for under €3

day_by_day.notes: Keep some euros handy for the bus transfer (approx €4-6 from Faro Airport). No major activities planned tonight - rest is priority after a long flight. Download the Rede Expressos app for budget bus travel around the Algarve.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely wake-up, walk down to the beachfront directly accessible from Aegean Bliss Resort. Explore the shoreline, take in the stunning September sea views, and enjoy the warm Algarve sun which is still strong in mid-September without peak summer crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local beach town on foot. Visit the nearest village market or local mercado for fresh fruit, cheese, and bread to stock up on affordable snacks. Spend the afternoon relaxing on the beach - September water temperatures are around 22°C, perfect for swimming.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the beachfront promenade at sunset. Find a local tasca (traditional tavern) for a budget dinner featuring fresh grilled fish - look for the 'prato do dia' (dish of the day) which is always the cheapest and freshest option.

meals.breakfast: Pick up pastries and coffee at a local padaria (bakery) - budget €3-4. Try a Galão (milky coffee) and croissant.
meals.lunch: Self-catered from the local market - bread, local cheese, fruit, and water for under €6 total
meals.dinner: Local tasca near the beach - grilled sardines or sea bream with rice and salad, prato do dia usually €7-10 including bread and water

day_by_day.notes: September is shoulder season in Algarve - prices are lower than July/August and beaches are less crowded. Sunscreen is still essential as UV index remains high. Check the resort's notice board for any free local events.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget local bus or rent a bicycle (€10-15/day) to visit one of the Algarve's most iconic beaches - Praia da Marinha or Praia de Benagil (depending on your resort's location near Lagoa/Carvoeiro area). Arrive early to secure a good spot and explore the dramatic limestone rock formations and sea caves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike along the coastal cliffs on the free Percurso dos Sete Vales Suspensos (Seven Hanging Valleys Trail) - a stunning 5.7km trail with breathtaking ocean views. This is completely free and one of the most spectacular walks in southern Europe. Bring water and snacks from your morning market purchases.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area and head to a local cervejaria (beer house) or marisqueira for affordable seafood. Try Amêijoas à Bulhão Pato (clams in garlic and white wine) as a starter with a cold Sagres or Super Bock beer.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast if included, or local café - coffee and toast with butter and jam for €2-3
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from yesterday's market supplies eaten on the clifftop trail - save money and enjoy the view
meals.dinner: Cervejaria or local seafood restaurant - budget €12-15 per person including a beer

day_by_day.notes: The Seven Hanging Valleys Trail is one of Portugal's most famous coastal walks. Wear sturdy shoes and bring at least 1.5L of water. The trail can be done as a loop or one-way with bus return. Check local bus schedules in advance at carris.pt or via the local tourist office.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip by local bus to Lagos - one of the Algarve's most charming historic towns. Explore the old town walls, the Slave Market Museum (Mercado de Escravos, €3 entry - world's first slave market), and the beautiful Igreja de Santo António church with its ornate gilded interior.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Ponta da Piedade - a spectacular headland with towering golden limestone sea stacks and grottos. You can hire a small boat tour of the grottos for around €15-20 or simply enjoy the free clifftop views. Then relax at Praia do Camilo, a beautiful small beach accessible via wooden steps.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Lagos town center in the early evening. Browse the pedestrianized Rua 25 de Abril for souvenir shopping and local craft stalls. Enjoy dinner at a local restaurant in Lagos before catching the last bus back.

meals.breakfast: Café in Lagos old town upon arrival - coffee and pastel de nata for €2
meals.lunch: Lagos market hall (Mercado Municipal) for fresh produce, or a budget lunch at a local snack bar - prego (steak sandwich) for €4-5
meals.dinner: Lagos restaurant - try Cataplana (traditional Algarvian seafood stew) which serves two people at €20-25 split between dining partners, or a grilled fish main for €10-12

day_by_day.notes: Bus from Algarve coastal towns to Lagos runs regularly via Rede Expressos - budget €5-8 return depending on your starting point. Lagos is very walkable once you arrive. The town gets lively in the evenings with a young traveler crowd - there are many affordable bars if you want to socialize.

day_by_day.morning: Wine tasting day! Research and visit a local Algarve winery. The Algarve has four DOC wine regions - look for wineries near your resort offering free or low-cost tastings. Quinta dos Vales near Estômbar or Adega do Cantor (Cliff Richard's winery near Guia) offer tours and tastings for €10-15 including multiple wine samples.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the wine theme with a visit to a local wine shop or adega (cellar) in the nearest town. Purchase a bottle or two of excellent local Algarve wine for €5-8 - great value. Spend the afternoon at the beach with your wine purchase and some local cheese and charcuterie for a budget picnic.
day_by_day.evening: Beach sunset picnic with your wine purchases from the afternoon. As darkness falls, head to a local restaurant for a light dinner or tapas-style petiscos (Portuguese small plates).

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the resort or local bakery - yogurt, fruit, and coffee for €3-4
meals.lunch: Light snacks at the winery during tasting, supplemented with market purchases
meals.dinner: Petiscos (Portuguese tapas) at a local bar-restaurant - order 3-4 small plates to share for €4-6 each, paired with local wine by the glass at €2-3

day_by_day.notes: Call ahead to book winery tours as some require reservations. The Algarve wine region is less famous than Douro or Alentejo but produces excellent, affordable wines especially from the Castelão and Negra Mole grape varieties. Ask for local recommendations at your resort reception.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Silves - the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve, a short bus ride inland. Explore the magnificent red sandstone Castelo de Silves (€2.80 entry) with panoramic views over the surrounding orange and almond orchards. The castle dates to the 8th century and is one of the best-preserved Moorish fortifications in Portugal.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Silves Cathedral (Sé Catedral de Silves, free entry) and wander the charming cobblestone streets of this authentic, non-touristy town. Visit the Museu Municipal de Arqueologia (€2 entry) to learn about the region's fascinating Moorish history. Browse the local market if it's a market day.
day_by_day.evening: Dine in Silves before returning - the town has excellent authentic restaurants at lower prices than coastal tourist areas. Try Restaurante Marisqueira Rui (famous for seafood cataplana) or a local tasca for traditional Algarvian cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Local café in Silves upon arrival - coffee and torrada (thick toast) for €2
meals.lunch: Silves market or a local snack bar - fresh orange juice (the region is famous for its oranges) and a sandwich for €4-5
meals.dinner: Traditional restaurant in Silves - grilled chicken piri-piri or fresh fish with local wine for €10-13 per person

day_by_day.notes: Silves is a refreshing change from the coastal tourist scene - prices are noticeably lower and the atmosphere is authentically Portuguese. The bus journey from coastal areas takes 30-60 minutes and costs €3-5. The town is particularly beautiful in September when the summer heat has eased slightly.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and beach morning at the resort's beachfront. This is your mid-trip relaxation day. Swim, sunbathe, read, and recharge. September beaches in the Algarve are wonderfully peaceful compared to summer. Explore the rock pools if your beach has them - the Algarve's golden limestone formations create fascinating tidal pools.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the immediate resort area more thoroughly on foot. Find hidden coves, local fishing spots, or clifftop viewpoints (miradouros) within walking distance of Aegean Bliss Resort. Chat with local fishermen if you encounter them - they often share tips on the best local spots.
day_by_day.evening: Cook a simple meal if your accommodation has kitchen facilities using ingredients from the local market - fresh fish, olive oil, garlic, and local vegetables. Alternatively, visit a local supermarket (Pingo Doce or Lidl are budget-friendly) and assemble a picnic dinner on the beach for the sunset.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at the resort or nearby café - full Portuguese breakfast with eggs, ham, cheese, toast, and coffee for €5-7
meals.lunch: Beach snacks - fruit, nuts, local chips, and a cold beer from a beach kiosk (quiosque) for €5-6
meals.dinner: Self-catered or supermarket picnic on the beach - fresh bread, rotisserie chicken (frango assado, €5-6 at supermarket), salad, and local wine for €10-12 total

day_by_day.notes: Pingo Doce and Lidl supermarkets offer excellent value in Portugal - their ready-made meals, fresh bread, and wine selections are great quality at low prices. Rotisserie chicken from Portuguese supermarkets is a legendary budget travel hack. This rest day is important for the second half of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente - the southwestern tip of continental Europe. Take an early bus to this dramatic, windswept headland. Visit the Fortaleza de Sagres (€3 entry) - a 15th-century fortress where Prince Henry the Navigator planned Portugal's Age of Discovery. The views from the cliffs are absolutely breathtaking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi (€5-7) to Cabo de São Vicente lighthouse - the most southwesterly point of mainland Europe. The 60-75m high cliffs are stunning and there's a small market selling local crafts and honey. Explore Praia do Beliche, a wild and beautiful beach below the fortress accessible via steep steps.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Sagres village for dinner before the return bus. The village is small but has good seafood restaurants catering to surfers and budget travelers. Try the local tuna (atum) which is caught fresh in these waters.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before departure - coffee and pastry at the resort or bus station café for €2-3
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Cabo de São Vicente with the most dramatic view in Portugal - bread, cheese, fruit, and water
meals.dinner: Sagres village restaurant - fresh tuna steak or grilled fish with local potatoes and salad for €10-13

day_by_day.notes: Sagres is about 30-45 minutes by bus from Lagos, so factor in the connection from your resort. The area is famous for surfing and has a laid-back, end-of-the-world atmosphere. Wind can be very strong at the cape - bring a light jacket even in September. This is one of the most memorable spots in all of Portugal.

day_by_day.morning: Second wine tasting experience - this time visit a different style of producer. Look for a cooperative winery (adega cooperativa) which often offers the most affordable tastings. The Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa is one of the Algarve's oldest and offers tastings for free or minimal cost. Focus on trying the local Medronho (strawberry tree brandy) - a unique Algarvian spirit.
day_by_day.afternoon: After wine tasting, visit the nearby town of Lagoa for some local exploration. Browse the weekly market if scheduled, visit the local church, and explore the whitewashed streets. Stop at a local deli (charcutaria) to pick up Algarvian specialties like smoked sausages, local honey, and fig-and-almond sweets (Dom Rodrigos) as souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area for a relaxed evening. Enjoy a sundowner drink on the beach or resort terrace with your Medronho or wine purchases. Find a local restaurant for a budget seafood dinner.

meals.breakfast: Café near the resort - fresh orange juice (squeezed to order), coffee, and toast for €3
meals.lunch: Lagoa market or local café - soup of the day (sopa do dia, €2-3) and bread, a very filling and cheap option
meals.dinner: Local restaurant near the resort - gambas al ajillo (garlic prawns) starter and grilled fish main with house wine for €13-15

day_by_day.notes: Medronho is a traditional Algarvian firewater made from the fruit of the strawberry tree - it's very strong (up to 48% ABV) but a unique local experience. Small bottles make great affordable souvenirs (€5-8). The Lagoa cooperative winery produces both red and white wines - the whites are particularly refreshing.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Albufeira - the Algarve's most famous resort town. Take the morning bus and explore the charming old town (the 'Fishermen's Quarter') which retains its authentic character despite the surrounding tourist development. Visit the clifftop Igreja Matriz and enjoy views over Praia dos Pescadores.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Albufeira's beaches - Praia de Albufeira (in town) or take the free beach train to Praia da Oura or Praia de Santa Eulália. These are beautiful golden sand beaches. Visit the local fish market if open to see the daily catch. Browse the Rua Cândido dos Reis for affordable local crafts and ceramics.
day_by_day.evening: Albufeira has an excellent range of affordable restaurants competing for business. Explore the old town's restaurant strips for the best value - look for places with handwritten menus in Portuguese (a sign of authenticity and value). Enjoy a lively evening atmosphere before the bus back.

meals.breakfast: Albufeira old town café upon arrival - galão and pastel de nata for €2
meals.lunch: Fish market area snack bar or old town restaurant - fresh grilled sardines with bread for €6-8 (September is still great sardine season)
meals.dinner: Old town Albufeira restaurant - half a grilled chicken (frango no churrasco) with fries and salad for €8-10, or a fresh fish option

day_by_day.notes: Albufeira can feel very touristy in its main strip area - stick to the old town for a more authentic and affordable experience. The beach train between beaches is free and a fun way to explore. Albufeira has a very lively nightlife if you want to socialize - many bars have happy hours from 5-8pm with 2-for-1 drinks.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Faro - the Algarve's capital city. Take the bus to Faro and spend the morning in the beautiful historic Cidade Velha (Old Town) surrounded by ancient Roman walls. Visit the impressive Sé Catedral de Faro (€3.50 entry including tower climb with panoramic views) and the charming Arco da Vila gateway.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Museu Municipal de Faro (€2 entry) housed in a former convent with Roman mosaics and local history exhibits. Then take the free or cheap ferry boat (€1.50-2 return) from Faro harbor to Ilha Deserta (Desert Island) or Ilha de Faro - pristine natural beaches within the Ria Formosa Natural Park, one of Portugal's most important wetland ecosystems.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Faro city center - the capital has excellent, authentic restaurants at reasonable prices. Explore the pedestrianized Rua de Santo António for dining options. Try Faro's local specialty of carob-based dishes or fresh tuna.

meals.breakfast: Faro city café - coffee and croissant or pastel de nata for €2
meals.lunch: Packed snacks on the island beach, or a beach kiosk on Ilha de Faro for a simple sandwich and drink for €5-6
meals.dinner: Faro restaurant in the pedestrian zone - fresh seafood pasta (massada de marisco) or a traditional Portuguese meat dish for €10-13

day_by_day.notes: The Ria Formosa Natural Park is one of Portugal's seven natural wonders - the ferry to the barrier islands is a highlight not to be missed. Birdwatching is excellent here with flamingos, spoonbills, and numerous migratory species in September. Faro Airport is nearby so this is also a good day to confirm your return flight details.

day_by_day.morning: Final beach morning - spend a leisurely last full day at your favorite beach discovered during the trip. Return to whichever beach impressed you most, whether it was the dramatic rock formations of Marinha, the wild beauty of Sagres, or the convenience of the resort beach. Swim, snorkel if you have equipment, and soak up the last of the Algarve sunshine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Souvenir shopping and last-minute exploration near the resort. Stock up on affordable Portuguese souvenirs - local honey (mel), fig and almond sweets (Dom Rodrigos, Morgados), ceramic azulejo tiles, cork products (Portugal produces 50% of the world's cork), and bottles of local wine or ginjinha. All available at local markets and shops for very reasonable prices.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at your favorite restaurant discovered during the trip, or try somewhere new for a special last-night meal. Treat yourself slightly - a nice bottle of Algarve wine, fresh lobster or prawns, and a dessert of Algarvian almond tart (tarte de amêndoa).

meals.breakfast: Leisurely café breakfast - full spread of coffee, fresh juice, toast, eggs, and pastries for €6-8
meals.lunch: Beach kiosk or snack bar for a last taste of casual Algarve dining - prego roll and a cold beer for €6-7
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner - slightly splurge at €15-20 per person for a memorable last meal with local wine, fresh seafood, and traditional dessert

day_by_day.notes: Pack your bags tonight as tomorrow is departure day. Check your resort checkout time and arrange any necessary transportation to the airport. Faro Airport is generally well-connected by bus. Keep some euros for airport coffee and any last-minute purchases. Weigh your luggage if you bought wine bottles - check airline liquid and weight restrictions.

day_by_day.morning: Check out from Aegean Bliss Resort. Store luggage at the resort if checkout is before your transport to the airport. Take a final walk on the beach for one last look at the Algarve coastline. Grab a coffee and pastel de nata at a local café for a final Portuguese moment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Faro Airport via local bus or pre-arranged transfer. Allow at least 2 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Browse the airport duty-free for any last-minute Portuguese wine, port, or ginjinha purchases - prices can be competitive for premium brands.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Portugal with wonderful memories of 13 days exploring the Algarve's stunning beaches, historic towns, and excellent wines. Review your trip and consider what you'd do differently or what you'd love to return to see.

meals.breakfast: Final Portuguese café breakfast near the resort - coffee and pastry for €3
meals.lunch: Airport café or restaurant - budget €8-12 for airport pricing, or bring snacks purchased earlier
meals.dinner: On the flight home or at your destination

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary for the 13-day trip: Accommodation at Aegean Bliss Resort (pre-booked), local bus transport €40-60 total, meals averaging €15-20/day = €195-260, activities and entrance fees €30-50, wine tastings €20-30, souvenirs €20-40. Estimated total spend excluding accommodation and flights: approximately €305-390 for a budget-conscious traveler. The Algarve offers exceptional value in September - you've experienced world-class beaches, historic culture, and excellent food and wine at very reasonable prices.

trip_options.title: Classic Portugal Algarve Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail from Benagil and descend to the secluded cove for swimming and snorkeling among rock arches.

experiences.name: Sagres Sunset & Cape St. Vincent Visit
experiences.description: Travel to the southwestern tip of Europe at Cape St. Vincent, a windswept promontory with a historic lighthouse and breathtaking Atlantic views. Explore the nearby Sagres Fortress, steeped in Age of Discovery history, and stay for one of the most spectacular sunsets on the continent.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30. Transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort (approx. 30–50 min drive depending on exact location). Check in, freshen up, and unwind with a welcome drink at the hotel bar if still open.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a light snack at the airport arrivals hall or a late-night bite at the hotel bar. Many Algarve resort bars serve tapas-style snacks until midnight.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 simple – no pre-booking needed. Confirm your transfer in advance (taxi or pre-arranged shuttle ~€30–50). Pack a snack for the ride just in case the hotel kitchen is closed upon arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a slow stroll along the beachfront to get your bearings and soak in the Algarve atmosphere. Dip your toes in the Atlantic for the first time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon relaxing on the resort beach or pool. Explore the immediate shoreline, rent a sunbed, and enjoy the warm September sea (avg. 22–24°C). Pick up a local map and plan the week ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the nearest town center for a casual first dinner out. Explore the promenade and enjoy the lively early-autumn atmosphere before returning to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort – included or ~€12–18 per person
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort beach bar – grilled fish sandwich or salad, ~€12–16
meals.dinner: A Tasca do Zé or similar local tasca (tavern) in the nearest town – try bacalhau à brás (salted cod) or grilled sardines, ~€18–25 per person with a glass of Alentejo wine

day_by_day.notes: September is ideal in the Algarve – crowds thin out after August, sea is warm, and prices drop slightly. Use this day to recover from travel and acclimate.

day_by_day.morning: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim: Set out early (9:00 AM) to beat the heat. Drive or take a local bus to Praia da Marinha (~30 min from most Algarve resort areas). Hike the dramatic clifftop trail with views of golden limestone arches and sea stacks. Stop at multiple lookout points for photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to Praia da Marinha beach itself – consistently ranked one of Europe's most beautiful. Swim in the crystal-clear turquoise water, explore the sea caves and rock formations by swimming or snorkeling. Bring water shoes as the beach is pebbly.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area and freshen up. Head to a nearby seafood restaurant for a celebratory first proper dinner. Watch the sunset over the Atlantic from a clifftop bar.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic or grab snacks from a local padaria (bakery) near Lagoa – pastel de nata, fresh bread, local cheese (~€8–10). There is a small café near the Marinha car park.
meals.dinner: O Terraço or similar clifftop restaurant near Carvoeiro – grilled sea bass (robalo) with roasted potatoes and salad, ~€22–30 per person including wine

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable hiking shoes and bring sunscreen, a hat, and at least 1.5L of water per person. The hike is moderate – about 5–7 km round trip on uneven cliff paths. Parking at Praia da Marinha fills up by 10 AM in September – arrive early or use the overflow lot.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Silves – the historic Moorish capital of the Algarve. Explore the striking red sandstone Castelo de Silves (€3 entry), walk the ancient walls, and visit the Gothic Cathedral (Sé de Silves). The town is a 30–45 min drive inland.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wine Tasting at Quinta dos Vales or Adega do Cantor (both near Silves/Lagoa area). These are among the Algarve's most acclaimed wineries. Book a guided tour and tasting session (~€15–25 per person) featuring local Algarve varietals including Negra Mole and Arinto. Many offer beautiful vineyard views.
day_by_day.evening: Dine in Silves before heading back. The town has excellent mid-range restaurants in the old quarter. Alternatively, stop at a local wine shop to pick up bottles to enjoy on the resort balcony.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or a pastelaria in town
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the winery restaurant or a café in Silves – cataplana de marisco (seafood stew) or prego (steak sandwich), ~€14–20
meals.dinner: Marisqueira Rui in Silves or similar – famous for shellfish platters and grilled meats, ~€20–28 per person with local wine

day_by_day.notes: Book the winery tour in advance – Quinta dos Vales and Adega do Cantor are popular and tours can fill up. September is harvest season (vindima) – you may even get to see or participate in grape picking, a special experience!

day_by_day.morning: Beach day at Praia de Benagil – famous for the iconic Benagil Sea Cave (Algar de Benagil). Arrive early by 9:00 AM. Book a kayak or stand-up paddleboard tour (€20–30) from the beach to paddle into the cathedral-like cave. Alternatively, join a boat tour (~€15) if paddling isn't preferred.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the cave visit, relax on Benagil Beach or take a short drive to Praia de Carvalho, a quieter neighboring beach accessible via a tunnel through the cliff. Spend the afternoon swimming and sunbathing.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a sunset swim. Enjoy a relaxed evening at the resort restaurant or nearby local spot.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before heading out
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at a beachside restaurant in Benagil village – grilled limpets (lapas), fresh fish of the day, ~€16–22
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant or a nearby casual spot – try amêijoas à bulhão pato (clams in garlic and white wine) as a starter, ~€20–25 per person

day_by_day.notes: Benagil Cave can only be entered by water (no land access). The kayak/SUP option gives you the most freedom. Tours book out fast on weekends – reserve online the day before. The sea inside the cave is calmer in the morning.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the local Sunday market (mercado) in the nearest town – many Algarve towns host weekly markets with fresh produce, local honey, almonds, figs, ceramics, and handmade goods. Stock up on local snacks and souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Albufeira Old Town – wander the whitewashed streets, visit the small fishing harbor, and browse boutique shops. The old town retains its charm even on busy weekends. Visit the small local church and enjoy the views from the clifftop lookout.
day_by_day.evening: Sagres Sunset & Cape St. Vincent Visit (evening version): If timing works, drive toward the western Algarve for a spectacular sunset at Cape St. Vincent (approx. 1.5–2 hr drive). The lighthouse at Europe's southwestern tip with the Atlantic crashing below is unforgettable at golden hour.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast at the Sunday market – fresh orange juice, tosta mista (ham and cheese toast), ~€5–8
meals.lunch: Picnic with market finds – local bread, cheese, presunto (cured ham), fresh figs, and a bottle of Algarve rosé, ~€12–15 total
meals.dinner: A Sagres restaurant near Cape St. Vincent area – try percebes (goose barnacles) and grilled tuna (atum), ~€22–28 per person, then drive back to resort

day_by_day.notes: Cape St. Vincent sunset is one of the most dramatic in Europe – locals and travelers gather to applaud as the sun dips below the horizon. Bring a light jacket as it can be windy and cool even in September. The drive back is about 2 hours – plan dinner early (6:30–7:00 PM) to return at a reasonable hour.

day_by_day.morning: Sagres Sunset & Cape St. Vincent Full Day Visit: Dedicate a full day to the far western Algarve. Start with the Fortaleza de Sagres (Sagres Fortress, €3 entry) – a dramatic fort perched on a clifftop with a mysterious wind compass (Rosa dos Ventos). Learn about Henry the Navigator's legendary navigation school.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Sagres peninsula – visit Praia do Beliche, a secluded beach tucked beneath towering cliffs accessible by stairs, and Praia de Sagres for a longer stretch of sand. Surf lessons are available here if interested (~€35–45 for a 2-hour beginner lesson). The Atlantic swells make Sagres a world-class surf destination.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the famous Cape St. Vincent sunset (second chance if you missed it on Day 6, or a wonderful repeat). The lighthouse gift shop sells local honey and ceramics. Drive back along the coast road for a scenic return.

meals.breakfast: Café in Sagres village – fresh pastries and galão (milky espresso), ~€5–7
meals.lunch: Restaurante A Sagres or Dromedário in Sagres – fresh tuna steak or cataplana, ~€16–22 per person
meals.dinner: Stop in Lagos on the way back for dinner – O Camilo or Restaurante Adega da Marina – try black pork (porco preto) from Alentejo or grilled dourada (sea bream), ~€20–28 per person

day_by_day.notes: Fill up on petrol before driving to Sagres as stations are limited. The Sagres area is noticeably cooler and windier than the eastern Algarve – pack an extra layer. Lagos is a beautiful town worth a quick evening stroll along its historic walls.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and resort morning – enjoy a slow breakfast, read by the pool, or treat yourself to a spa treatment at the Aegean Bliss Resort if available (~€50–80 for a massage). This is a deliberate rest day mid-trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local area on foot or by bike. Rent bicycles (~€10–15/day) and cycle along the coast path or through nearby villages. Visit a local quinta (farm) if one is nearby for fresh produce or olive oil tasting.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a clifftop bar near the resort. Try a local medronho (arbutus berry firewater) cocktail or a glass of vinho verde. Dinner at a mid-range restaurant in the resort area.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a local café – bifanas (pork sandwiches) or fresh soup, ~€8–12
meals.dinner: Tasca or cervejaria (beer hall) near the resort – mixed seafood grill or arroz de lingueirão (razor clam rice), ~€18–24 per person

day_by_day.notes: Mid-trip rest days are essential for a balanced itinerary. Use this time to do laundry, recharge devices, review photos, and plan any remaining bookings for the second week.

day_by_day.morning: Wine Tasting Day 2 – Visit Herdade dos Grous or Quinta da Tôr (near Loulé/Boliqueime area, ~30 min inland). These estates offer a more intimate wine experience with organic and biodynamic wines. Book a morning tour (10:00 AM) with a guided vineyard walk and barrel tasting.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the winery, explore the charming hilltop village of Alte – considered one of the prettiest villages in the Algarve. Walk through cobblestone streets, visit the 16th-century church, and cool off at the natural freshwater springs (Fontes de Alte) – perfect for a refreshing dip.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the coast for dinner. Try a different cuisine tonight for variety – there are excellent international options in most Algarve resort towns alongside traditional Portuguese.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Winery lunch pairing – most estates offer a cheese, charcuterie, and wine pairing lunch for ~€25–35 per person, excellent value
meals.dinner: Tasca do Celeiro in Loulé or a restaurant in the resort area – try carne de porco à alentejana (pork with clams), ~€18–25 per person

day_by_day.notes: Alte's springs can be crowded on weekends – a Wednesday visit is ideal. Bring a swimsuit and towel for the natural pools. The winery visit + Alte combo makes for one of the most culturally rich inland days in the Algarve.

day_by_day.morning: Ria Formosa Natural Park boat tour – head east toward Faro. Join a guided boat tour through the Ria Formosa lagoon system (~€25–35 per person, 2.5–3 hours). Visit barrier islands, spot flamingos, herons, and other migratory birds. Stop at Ilha Deserta for a short walk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Faro Old Town (Cidade Velha) – walk through the Roman and Moorish walls, visit the Sé Cathedral (climb the tower for panoramic views, €3), and browse the Museu Municipal de Faro. Faro is often overlooked but has genuine Portuguese charm away from tourist crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Faro before returning to the resort. The area around Faro Marina has excellent restaurants with views over the lagoon.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Fresh oysters and clams at a Ria Formosa seafood shack on one of the islands – a unique experience, ~€15–20
meals.dinner: Restaurante Faz Gostos or Tasca do Ricky in Faro – try linguado grelhado (grilled sole) or arroz de lingueirão, ~€20–28 per person with local white wine

day_by_day.notes: Book the Ria Formosa boat tour in advance – several operators depart from Faro Marina and Olhão. The lagoon is a UNESCO-listed ecosystem and one of Portugal's most important wetlands. Bring binoculars if you have them for birdwatching.

day_by_day.morning: Beach hopping day – explore some of the Algarve's lesser-known beaches. Visit Praia do Camilo (Lagos area) – a small, sheltered cove with dramatic cliff staircase access. Then drive to Praia da Luz for a longer, calmer beach more popular with locals.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a final proper beach afternoon. Rent a paddleboard or kayak from the resort beach (~€15–20/hr) and explore the coastline from the water. Swim, snorkel, or simply relax – this is your last full beach afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Special dinner night – treat yourself to the best restaurant in the resort area. Many Algarve restaurants offer tasting menus with wine pairings for €45–65 per person – a splurge-worthy experience for a Friday night.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Beach café at Praia da Luz – grilled chicken piri-piri or fresh fish tacos, ~€14–18
meals.dinner: Upscale local restaurant – tasting menu with Algarve wine pairing featuring local seafood, black pork, and traditional desserts like Dom Rodrigo (almond and egg sweet), ~€45–65 per person

day_by_day.notes: Praia do Camilo has limited parking – arrive before 10 AM or after 4 PM. The cliff staircase is steep but the beach is worth it. Book the tasting menu dinner at least 2 days in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Saturday market in Loulé – the largest and most authentic market in the Algarve. The permanent market building is a beautiful Moorish-style structure. Buy last-minute gifts: local almonds, carob products, flavored salts, ceramics, and handmade leather goods.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final wine experience – visit a local adega (wine shop/cellar) in the resort town for a self-guided tasting of Algarve wines to buy. Alternatively, take a cooking class (~€60–80 per person) to learn to make cataplana and pastel de nata – a wonderful skill to take home.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at your favorite restaurant from the trip, or try something new. Enjoy a final sunset walk along the beach. Pack your bags and prepare for departure.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast at the Loulé market – fresh pastries and espresso
meals.lunch: Market lunch – buy fresh bread, local cheese, olives, and charcuterie for a market picnic, ~€10–15
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a favorite restaurant or the resort restaurant – splurge on a bottle of Algarve Reserva wine, ~€25–35 per person

day_by_day.notes: Loulé market is busiest between 9–11 AM on Saturdays. Go early for the best selection. Many vendors accept card payments but bring some cash for smaller stalls. Shipping wine home: most wine shops can arrange shipping, or buy padded wine carriers for your luggage.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning – wake up early for one last sunrise walk on the beach. Take photos, collect a few shells, and say goodbye to the Algarve coastline. Enjoy a final resort breakfast at leisure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort (standard checkout 11:00 AM – confirm with hotel). If your flight is in the afternoon or evening, store luggage at the hotel and spend a final couple of hours at the beach or pool. Drive to Faro Airport (allow 45–60 min plus time for fuel return and check-in).
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Faro Airport. Browse the airport duty-free for final Portuguese souvenirs – Pastéis de Belém tins, ginjinha liqueur, or Vinho Verde. Carry home golden memories of the Algarve.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast – enjoy every bite
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café near the resort or at Faro Airport – soup and sandwich, ~€10–14
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or on the flight

day_by_day.notes: Faro Airport (FAO) is small and efficient but gets busy on Sunday afternoons in September. Arrive 2.5 hours before departure. Return your rental car with a full tank – petrol stations near the airport are easy to find. Don't forget to check for any items left in the hotel safe!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Portugal Algarve Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail from Benagil and descend to the secluded cove for swimming and snorkeling among rock arches.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour
experiences.description: Visit local wineries in the Lagoa DOC wine region, the heart of Algarve winemaking. Tour the vineyards, learn about indigenous grape varieties like Negra Mole and Crato Branco, and enjoy guided tastings of regional whites, reds, and the famous Algarve medronho brandy paired with local cheeses.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle by kayak through the iconic Benagil Cave, one of the most photographed sea caves in the world. A guided tour takes you through hidden grottos, natural arches, and secluded beaches only accessible by water, offering a unique perspective of the Algarve's dramatic coastline.

experiences.name: Sagres Sunset & Cape St. Vincent Visit
experiences.description: Travel to the southwestern tip of Europe at Cape St. Vincent, a windswept promontory with a historic lighthouse and breathtaking Atlantic views. Explore the nearby Sagres Fortress, steeped in Age of Discovery history, and stay for one of the most spectacular sunsets on the continent.

experiences.name: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat & Seafood Experience
experiences.description: Take a guided boat tour through the Ria Formosa lagoon system, a protected natural park teeming with wildlife and barrier islands. Stop at a traditional oyster and clam farm for a tasting straight from the water, then visit the pristine Ilha Deserta beach, accessible only by boat.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. A pre-arranged private luxury transfer whisks you to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, enjoy a welcome glass of Algarve sparkling wine prepared by the concierge, and settle into your beachfront suite.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Light late-night room service at the resort — charcuterie board with local cheeses, Alentejo cured meats, olives, and a bottle of chilled Vinho Verde to unwind after the flight.

day_by_day.notes: Ensure private airport transfer is pre-booked through the resort concierge. Request early check-in amenities: chilled towels, welcome fruit basket, and turndown service. No alarm needed — rest is the priority tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely resort breakfast on the terrace overlooking the Atlantic. Spend the morning exploring the resort's beachfront — take a private stretch of beach walk, dip in the infinity pool, and get acquainted with the Algarve's golden coastline. Meet with the resort concierge to review and confirm the full 13-day itinerary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation afternoon: stroll through the nearest coastal village, browse artisan shops for local ceramics and cork goods, and enjoy a poolside lounge session. Arrange a private yoga or spa session at the resort to recover from travel fatigue.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's clifftop bar, sipping on a Gin & Tónica with fresh local botanicals. Dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast buffet on the sea-view terrace — fresh pastries, local honey, smoked fish, tropical fruits, and made-to-order eggs.
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the resort — grilled sea bass with lemon and herbs, a fresh salad, and sparkling water.
meals.dinner: Resort signature restaurant: tasting menu featuring Algarve cataplana (seafood stew), grilled tiger prawns, and a curated selection of local wines from the Lagoa DOC region.

day_by_day.notes: This is a recovery and orientation day. Avoid over-scheduling. Ask the concierge about September sea temperatures — typically a warm 22–24°C, perfect for swimming throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim — depart the resort after breakfast for the short drive to Praia da Marinha, consistently rated one of Europe's most beautiful beaches. Join a private guided coastal hike along the dramatic golden limestone cliffs, exploring hidden sea arches, grottos, and panoramic viewpoints. The guide will share geological and cultural history of the Algarve coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to Praia da Marinha's crystalline turquoise waters for a private swim and snorkeling session. Relax on the beach with premium sunbeds and a personal beach butler service arranged in advance. Explore the nearby rock pools and smaller coves accessible only on foot.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a sunset shower and refresh. Head to a renowned local seafood restaurant in the Carvoeiro or Lagoa area for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — freshly baked croissants, açaí bowls, smoked salmon, and Portuguese espresso.
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic basket prepared by the resort chef, enjoyed on the cliffs above Praia da Marinha — artisan sandwiches, local cheeses, fresh fruit, and chilled rosé wine.
meals.dinner: Restaurant O Castelo or equivalent premium seafood restaurant in Carvoeiro: whole grilled lobster, percebes (barnacles), and a bottle of Algarve white wine.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable hiking shoes with grip for the coastal trail. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, and a light layer for the clifftop breeze. The hike is moderate — approximately 3–4 km round trip with some uneven terrain.

day_by_day.morning: Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour — depart after a leisurely breakfast for a full-day private wine experience in the Lagoa DOC wine region, the heart of Algarve winemaking. Begin with a guided tour of a premier estate, exploring the vineyards, learning about indigenous grape varieties such as Negra Mole and Crato Branco, and visiting the cellar for a barrel-tasting experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to a second boutique winery for a formal seated wine tasting paired with regional appetizers. A sommelier guides you through five to seven wines, discussing terroir, production methods, and food pairing philosophy. Optionally visit a third producer specializing in Algarve medronho (arbutus berry spirit) for a unique artisan tasting.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort in the late afternoon. Freshen up and enjoy a quiet evening on your private terrace with a bottle of your favorite wine purchased during the tour.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — Portuguese egg tarts (pastéis de nata), fresh orange juice, yogurt with local fig jam, and espresso.
meals.lunch: Wine estate lunch: a curated farm-to-table spread of local charcuterie, artisan bread, regional cheeses, fig preserves, and paired wines served under a pergola in the vineyard.
meals.dinner: In-resort private dining on your beachfront terrace — a chef's special three-course dinner with wine pairings from the day's discoveries, arranged through the concierge.

day_by_day.notes: A private driver is essential for this day — arrange through the resort. Do not plan any physically demanding activities the following morning. Purchase a selection of wines at the estate; the resort can store them properly and arrange international shipping if desired.

day_by_day.morning: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour — after breakfast, transfer to Praia de Benagil for a private guided kayak tour through the iconic Benagil Cave, one of the world's most photographed sea caves. A professional guide leads you through the dramatic sea arches and into the cathedral-like cave interior, where a natural skylight illuminates the golden sand below.
day_by_day.afternoon: Following the kayak tour, explore the surrounding coastline by sea kayak, discovering hidden grottoes, arched rock formations, and secluded beaches accessible only from the water. Return to shore and relax at a nearby beach club with premium loungers and cocktail service.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a clifftop bar overlooking the Benagil coastline, then transfer to an upscale restaurant in Armação de Pêra or Portimão for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — avocado toast on sourdough, poached eggs, fresh fruit platter, and cold-pressed juice.
meals.lunch: Post-kayak lunch at a beachside premium restaurant near Benagil — grilled octopus salad, fresh clam rice (arroz de amêijoas), and local craft beer or sparkling water.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Sueste in Ferragudo or equivalent: river-facing terrace dining with grilled fresh fish of the day, cataplana de marisco, and a curated Algarve wine list.

day_by_day.notes: Kayaking requires moderate fitness. Bring a waterproof bag for valuables, apply waterproof sunscreen, and wear a rash guard or swimwear. The cave is best visited in the morning when light enters the skylight most dramatically — confirm timing with the guide. Avoid this activity if sea conditions are rough.

day_by_day.morning: Spa and wellness morning at the Aegean Bliss Resort. Book a signature two-hour treatment — choose from a deep tissue massage, a traditional hammam experience, or a marine algae body wrap using locally sourced Atlantic seaweed. Follow with time in the thermal pools, steam room, and relaxation lounge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private yacht charter departure from the nearest marina (Portimão or Vilamoura). Spend the afternoon cruising the Algarve coastline aboard a luxury sailing yacht, anchoring at secluded coves for swimming and snorkeling. Onboard catering with chilled champagne, fresh fruit, and seafood canapés.
day_by_day.evening: Return to marina at sunset with golden light over the Atlantic. Transfer back to the resort for a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-spa breakfast — granola, Greek yogurt, fresh berries, herbal tea, and fresh-squeezed orange juice.
meals.lunch: Onboard the yacht — a luxury catered spread of smoked salmon blinis, chilled lobster, artisan cheeses, crusty bread, and Champagne or chilled Alvarinho white wine.
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant or nearby fine-dining venue: slow-roasted Alentejo black pork (porco preto), seasonal vegetables, and a robust Douro red wine.

day_by_day.notes: Book the yacht charter at least one week in advance through the resort concierge. Specify the number of guests, preferred duration (4–6 hours recommended), and any dietary requirements for catering. Bring a light jacket for the return sail as evenings can be breezy on the water in September.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the historic city of Silves — transfer by private car to explore the Algarve's ancient Moorish capital. Begin with a guided tour of the impressive red sandstone Silves Castle (Castelo de Silves), one of the best-preserved Moorish fortifications in Portugal, with panoramic views over orange groves and the Arade River valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Silves' charming old town: visit the Gothic cathedral, browse artisan shops, and stop at the Museu Municipal de Arqueologia. In the late afternoon, visit a premium local cork factory for a behind-the-scenes tour of Portugal's world-famous cork industry — a unique and educational experience.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Silves at a celebrated local restaurant before returning to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — full Portuguese spread with fresh bread, local honey, soft cheeses, cured ham, and galão coffee.
meals.lunch: Restaurante Marisqueira Rui in Silves or equivalent: traditional Algarve cuisine — grilled sardines, orange and fennel salad, and local Silves white wine.
meals.dinner: Café Inglês in Silves or a premium restaurant in the castle quarter: slow-braised lamb with chickpeas, almond and fig dessert, and a glass of aged Alentejo wine.

day_by_day.notes: Silves is approximately 30–40 minutes from the central Algarve by private car. The castle grounds can be warm in the afternoon — visit in the morning when it is cooler. September is the tail end of Silves' tourist season, so it will be less crowded than July–August.

day_by_day.morning: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat & Seafood Experience — depart early by private transfer to Faro (approximately 45–60 minutes east) to join a private guided boat tour through the Ria Formosa lagoon system, a UNESCO-protected natural park. Glide through tidal channels, salt marshes, and barrier islands teeming with flamingos, herons, and migratory shorebirds. The guide provides expert commentary on the unique ecosystem.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disembark on one of the remote barrier islands (Ilha Deserta or Ilha do Farol) for a private beach experience. Swim in calm, shallow turquoise lagoon waters, relax on pristine white sands, and enjoy a fresh seafood lunch at the island's renowned restaurant. Return by boat in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Faro's old town (Cidade Velha) briefly — walk through the medieval city walls, visit the Arco da Vila, and browse the marina before transferring back to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast — energy-boosting spread of eggs, whole grain toast, smoked fish, fresh fruit, and strong Portuguese coffee.
meals.lunch: Restaurante Estamine on Ilha Deserta (or equivalent island restaurant): legendary fresh oysters, clams à Bulhão Pato, grilled fish of the day, and a crisp Algarve white wine with feet in the sand.
meals.dinner: Resort dinner or delivery of premium local seafood to your suite — relaxed evening after a full day of exploration.

day_by_day.notes: Book the private boat tour through a reputable Faro-based operator in advance. Bring binoculars for birdwatching, reef-safe sunscreen, and a light layer for the boat journey. Ilha Deserta restaurant is seasonal — confirm availability for September. This is one of the most memorable days of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Sagres Sunset & Cape St. Vincent Visit — depart after breakfast for the western Algarve on a full-day private excursion. Drive through the Costa Vicentina, a wild and rugged Atlantic coastline protected within the Southwest Alentejo and Vicentine Coast Natural Park. Stop at Praia do Amado, a world-class surf beach, to watch professional surfers and take in the dramatic scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Cape St. Vincent (Cabo de São Vicente), the southwestern tip of continental Europe. Explore the historic lighthouse, walk the windswept clifftops with sheer 75-metre drops into the Atlantic, and absorb the profound sense of standing at the edge of the known world. Continue to the nearby Sagres Fortress (Fortaleza de Sagres) for a guided tour of this historic navigational stronghold linked to the Age of Discovery.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from Cape St. Vincent — renowned as one of the most spectacular sunsets in Europe, with the sun sinking into the Atlantic horizon. Dinner in Sagres village before the return journey.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — smoked salmon bagels, cream cheese, capers, fresh orange juice, and espresso for an energizing start to a long day.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch on the cliffs near Cape St. Vincent or at a local café in Sagres — fresh tuna sandwiches, local cheese, fruit, and sparkling water.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Vila Velha in Sagres or equivalent: premium fresh tuna (the region is famous for it), grilled sea bream, and a bottle of local wine before the scenic drive back to the resort.

day_by_day.notes: Cape St. Vincent is approximately 1.5–2 hours from the central Algarve. Bring a windproof jacket — the cape is extremely windy year-round regardless of temperature. The sunset here in September typically occurs around 19:30–20:00. This is a full and rewarding day; plan for a late return to the resort.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery and resort indulgence morning. Sleep in, enjoy breakfast in bed, and spend the morning at the resort's private beach. Arrange a private paddleboard or stand-up paddleboard (SUP) lesson with the resort's water sports team, exploring the calm September waters along the beachfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the resort's spa for a rejuvenating facial or couples' treatment. Alternatively, take a private guided e-bike tour of the surrounding coastal countryside — vineyards, carob and almond orchards, and traditional Algarvian villages with whitewashed chimneys.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset wine tasting on your private terrace — arrange a curated selection of Algarve and Alentejo wines delivered by the resort sommelier, paired with local charcuterie and artisan cheeses.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast in bed — full resort service with fresh pastries, fruit, eggs Benedict, and freshly squeezed juices.
meals.lunch: Resort beach club: lobster roll, truffle fries, and a glass of chilled Champagne under a private cabana.
meals.dinner: Premium restaurant in the nearby town of Albufeira or Lagos: innovative Portuguese cuisine — duck rice (arroz de pato), salt cod (bacalhau) prepared in a contemporary style, and a fine Douro red.

day_by_day.notes: This is a flexible, low-key day intentionally placed mid-trip to recharge. Customize based on energy levels and personal preferences. The resort concierge can arrange any last-minute experiences or reservations for the remaining days.

day_by_day.morning: Private cooking class with a local Algarve chef — arrange through the resort concierge for a morning immersion into Portuguese coastal cuisine. Visit a local market first to select the freshest ingredients: fresh fish, clams, local vegetables, almonds, figs, and carob. Return to a private kitchen space to prepare a traditional cataplana, açorda de mariscos (seafood bread stew), and almond-based desserts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy the fruits of your culinary labor at a leisurely sit-down lunch. Afterward, spend the afternoon at leisure — explore a nearby coastal town such as Lagos, known for its stunning beaches, historic city walls, and vibrant arts scene. Visit Ponta da Piedade, a spectacular series of sea stacks and arches just outside Lagos.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk along the Lagos promenade. Dinner at one of Lagos' finest restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-market breakfast at the resort — yogurt parfait, fresh fruit, and espresso.
meals.lunch: The dishes you prepared during the cooking class, enjoyed with local wine in a beautiful setting — a uniquely personal and memorable meal.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina in Lagos or equivalent: premium seafood and traditional Portuguese dishes in an elegant setting overlooking the marina, with a carefully selected wine pairing.

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class at least 3–4 days in advance. Ponta da Piedade near Lagos is best visited in late afternoon when the golden light enhances the rock formations. Wear comfortable shoes for the cliff walk. Lagos is approximately 30–40 minutes from the central Algarve resort area.

day_by_day.morning: Second Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour — return to the Lagoa DOC wine region to explore producers not visited on Day 4. Focus this visit on a premium estate offering a vertical tasting of aged vintages, a private meeting with the winemaker, and an exclusive tour of the estate's historic adega (winery). Consider visiting Quinta dos Vales, known for its sculpture garden and award-winning wines.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the winery tour, stop at a local artisan market or deli to purchase fine Algarve products to take home: premium olive oil, local honey, medronho, wine, and dried figs. Return to the resort for a relaxed late afternoon by the pool.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell pre-dinner cocktails at the resort's bar, reflecting on the journey. Special farewell dinner at the resort or at the finest restaurant in the region.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — full spread with special request for freshly made French toast with local fig compote and mascarpone.
meals.lunch: Winery estate lunch — a long, leisurely table under the vines with local bread, regional cheeses, charcuterie, roasted almonds, and a flight of the estate's finest wines.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at the resort's finest restaurant or at a Michelin-recognized establishment in the Algarve: multi-course tasting menu showcasing the best of Portuguese cuisine — from Atlantic seafood to Alentejo meats — with a premium wine pairing curated by the head sommelier.

day_by_day.notes: Request a personalized wine tasting card or certificate from the estate as a keepsake. Consider arranging international shipping of wine purchases directly from the estate. Confirm farewell dinner reservations at least 48 hours in advance and inform the restaurant it is your last evening — they may offer a special touch.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Algarve — wake early for one last sunrise walk on the beach. Take a slow, mindful breakfast on your private terrace, savoring the Atlantic view. Pack and prepare for departure. Arrange a final spa treatment or pool session if time allows before checkout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Depending on your departure flight time, consider a final stop at a scenic viewpoint, a last coffee at a local café, or a quick browse of a souvenir shop in the nearest town for any remaining gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Private luxury transfer to Faro Airport for your departure flight. Carry the memories of 13 extraordinary days in the Algarve — golden cliffs, crystalline waters, world-class wine, and the warmth of Portuguese hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — a special farewell spread ordered the night before: your personal favorites from the week, fresh pastries, and a glass of sparkling wine to toast the journey.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café near the airport or a premium airport lounge meal — fresh sandwiches, salads, and a final glass of Algarve wine.
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or at destination.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange the airport transfer with the resort concierge the evening before. Allow at least 2.5 hours before your flight for check-in and security at Faro Airport, especially during the September shoulder season when the airport remains busy. Confirm all wine and souvenir purchases are properly packed for safe transit. Request a late checkout from the resort if your flight departs in the evening.
